thread.title: Close Update: Event Risk and Revenue Warnings Weigh on Wall Street

author: MT Newswires
title: Close Update: Event Risk and Revenue Warnings Weigh on Wall Street
text:
Shutterstock photo The major market indices were off their session lows but still closed with sizable losses on Monday as revenue warnings from Caterpillar ( CAT ) and Nvidia ( NVDA ) coupled with escalating tensions between the US and China as Washington prepares criminal charges against Huawei eroded confidence on Wall Street. Led by losses in the technology and energy sectors, the S&P 500 closed lower for the first time in four days.
In the wake of China's downbeat industrial profits data overnight, Caterpillar and Nvidia warned that FY19 results could be negatively impacted by "deteriorating macro economic conditions", unleashing a flight-to-safety that drove the Dow Jones Industrial Average as much as 400 points lower.
Event risk also fueled Monday's early losses with investors bracing for Tuesday's Brexit vote in the UK, the Federal Open Market Committee meeting Wednesday, US/China trade talks and a deluge of corporate results. A very eventful week ends with January non-farm payrolls Friday.
Demand for safety drove gold prices more than $5 higher per ounce despite the weaker dollar, and Treasury yields lower across the belly of the yield curve. Oil futures tanked on supply pressures and the political crisis in Venezuela, although oil recouped some lost ground late in the day after the US Treasury announced sanctions against state-owned PDVSA.
Bullish economic data failed to dent the bearish price action on Wall Street even as the Chicago Fed national activity index rose to a 4-month high, and the Dallas Fed manufacturing index was jerked into positive territory.
On Tuesday's calendar is international trade in goods, the Case Shiller home price index, consumer confidence, as well as an auction of 52-week Treasury bills, 2-year floating rate notes and 7-yr notes. Earnings announced tomorrow include 3M ( MMM ), Harley-Davidson ( HOG ), Lockheed Martin ( LMT ), Pfizer (PFE) and Verizon (VZ) with Apple (AAPL) and Ebay (EBAY) reporting after the close.
